intent: Product side nav: brand header, icon items, optional badges, closeable; preset props or compose your own from SideNav.Root/Header/Brand/Toggle/Nav/Section/Item blocks. Not AppNav. Not an overlay itself: below 64rem AppShellPattern (app-shell) puts it inside kit Drawer.
doNotUseWhen: Product top bar with logo and search — use AppHeader

title.note: Brand title in the header. Accessible name on the aside when showHeader is false

mark.note: Brand letter. Defaults to the first character of title

showHeader.note: Brand mark, title, and close. Set false when AppHeader already provides brand. Rail open/close is controlled by `open`.

radius.note: Rail corners. md is radius-surface-md. none is a flush square column next to AppHeader.

side.note: Does not position SideNav. The consumer shell uses row-reverse for right

groups.note: SideNavGroup[]: { label, items: SideNavItemData[] }. Takes precedence over items

items.note: SideNavItemData[] (id, label, href, onClick, icon, active, disabled, badge, items). icon: any Lucide name or a Lucide component (client code only; from a Server Component use a name). Flat list when groups is omitted. Leaf onClick is in-app select; href is a link when onClick is omitted.

footer.note: SideNavItemData, SideNavItemData[] (e.g. Settings), or any ReactNode such as an account card.

header.note: Replaces the brand (mark + title) in the header. The preset keeps a SideNav.Toggle beside it: Close while open; on the closed rail the slot fades and goes inert and the Toggle moves to the start edge to reopen the rail. For a mark inside a custom header, build it from blocks with SideNav.Brand. Ignored when showHeader is false.

beforeGroups.note: Pinned above the scrolling groups, e.g. a workspace switcher. Faded and inert on the closed rail.

afterGroups.note: Pinned below the scrolling groups, above the footer, e.g. a promo card. Faded and inert on the closed rail.

renderItem.note: (item, defaultNode) => ReactNode. Customise one row. defaultNode is the kit link or button with aria-current and disclosure attributes: wrap it, put content beside it, or cloneElement it with new children. Keep it in the tree. Applies to nested and footer rows too.

passthrough.note: aria-label defaults to title and can be overridden.

compose.note: The data props above are the preset. Build your own nav from these blocks; the preset is built from them (SideNav.Brand + SideNav.Toggle in its header). Dot access (SideNav.Root) in client components; named exports (SideNavRoot, SideNavBrand, SideNavItem, …) in Server Components, which cannot dot into a client module. SideNavItem is the row component; the preset row data type is SideNavItemData. Every block takes ref, className and native attributes (K22).

SideNav.Root.props: open, defaultOpen, onOpenChange, side, radius, aria-label
SideNav.Root.note: Owns open/closed state (context). ref/className/rest on the aside. aria-label names the aside and is the default name of SideNav.Nav.

SideNav.Header.note: Top bar. Put SideNav.Brand (or a workspace switcher) and SideNav.Toggle as direct children. With a Toggle inside, everything else in the header fades and leaves the tab order on the closed rail, except SideNav.Brand's mark.

SideNav.Brand.element: button.mark + p.title (direct children of SideNav.Header, no wrapper)
SideNav.Brand.props: title (node), mark (letter or node; defaults to the first character of a string title), openLabel (default Open)
SideNav.Brand.note: The preset's brand. On the closed rail the title fades and the mark stays at the start edge, centred on the icon axis; clicking it reopens the rail (aria-label openLabel). While open the mark is disabled and aria-hidden. A SideNav.Toggle in the same header hides on the closed rail instead of moving, so the mark is the one reopen control. ref/className/rest go to the mark button. Reopening via the mark moves focus to the header's Toggle (else the first nav row).

SideNav.Toggle.note: Closes the open rail; on the closed rail it moves to the start edge and reopens it. Beside a SideNav.Brand it hides on the closed rail instead (the mark reopens). ref/rest to the button. onClick runs first; preventDefault skips the toggle. Reopening keeps focus on it (now Close).

SideNav.Slot.note: Pinned outside the scroll (switcher, promo, pinned rows). Faded and inert on the closed rail unless keepOnRail.

SideNav.Nav.note: The scrolling navigation landmark. aria-label defaults to the root's aria-label.

SideNav.Section.note: Optional caption plus the list of rows. Without label it is just the list (use it to wrap footer rows).

SideNav.Item.props: label (string), icon (any Lucide name — curated instant, others on demand — a Lucide component, or a node; from a Server Component pass a name or element, not a component reference), badge, active, disabled, href, onClick, defaultExpanded, children
SideNav.Item.note: active → aria-current=page and the active fill. href → link; onClick → button. Nested SideNav.Item children → disclosure button with aria-expanded/aria-controls (one level). ref/className/rest go to the row control, not the li. On the closed rail the label shows in a kit Tooltip automatically.

SideNav.Footer.note: Bottom bar: a SideNav.Section of rows or any node (account card).

compose.hook: useSideNav() → { open, rail, setOpen, toggle, side } inside SideNav.Root, for a custom toggle or rail-aware content.
compose.snippet:
<SideNav.Root aria-label="Agentix">
  <SideNav.Header>
    <SideNav.Brand title="Agentix" />
    <SideNav.Toggle />
  </SideNav.Header>
  <SideNav.Slot>
    <DropdownMenu triggerStyle="field" size="sm" ariaLabel="Workspace" trigger="Personal" groups={workspaces} />
  </SideNav.Slot>
  <SideNav.Nav>
    <SideNav.Section label="Workspace">
      <SideNav.Item label="Overview" icon="House" href="/" active />
      <SideNav.Item label="Projects" icon="Folder">
        <SideNav.Item label="Launch" href="/projects/launch" />
      </SideNav.Item>
    </SideNav.Section>
  </SideNav.Nav>
  <SideNav.Footer>
    <SideNav.Section><SideNav.Item label="Settings" icon="Settings" href="/settings" /></SideNav.Section>
  </SideNav.Footer>
</SideNav.Root>

cssVars.--sidenav-width: Open width of the rail and its inner panel (layout-sidebar)
cssVars.--sidenav-width-collapsed: Closed rail width (layout-sidebar-compact). AppHeader's brand column follows it unless --appheader-brand-width is set, so set it on :root to move both
cssVars.--sidenav-item-padding: Row padding; sets row height and the closed-rail icon chip (space-inset-sm)
cssVars.--sidenav-item-gap: Gap between rows, top level and submenu (space-stack-2xs)
cssVars.--sidenav-item-active-background: Active row fill and active badge fill (surface-brand-subtle)
cssVars.--sidenav-item-active-text: Active row and active badge text (text-brand)

requirements: In-flow aside, not a dialog and not position:fixed
No overlay, no focus trap, no Escape-to-close
Close is a kit Button with PanelLeftClose or PanelRightClose and ariaLabel Close
Closed rail reopens via the brand mark button (SideNav.Brand) with ariaLabel Open (openLabel); while open the mark is disabled, aria-hidden and out of the tab order
Title is visible in the header when open; clipped when closed
When showHeader is false, omit the header and close; title remains the accessible name via aria-label
Active leaf uses aria-current=page
Parent with nested items is a disclosure with aria-expanded
Closed rail clips labels via overflow; labels stay in the DOM for assistive tech
Outer shell width animates; inner panel stays at layout-sidebar width so icons do not recenter
Closed rail trailing border is on the outer shell — the inner panel is clipped
Closed rail must not change item width or height — size snaps cause open/close jump
Closed rail paints a square chip over the icon; do not clip a full-width row background
List items keep space-stack-2xs between rows so selected and hover surfaces do not touch
renderItem keeps defaultNode in the tree so aria-current and aria-expanded stay on the row
Slot content is inert on the closed rail so clipped controls are not focusable
Closed rail: every Item names itself in a kit Tooltip (placed outside the rail edge)
SideNav.Toggle stays visible and focusable on the closed rail and reopens it, unless a SideNav.Brand sits in the same header: then the Toggle is hidden there and the mark reopens

A user reopen (mark or Toggle, pointer or keyboard) moves focus to the visible Toggle (Close), else the first focusable nav row; programmatic open changes do not move focus. Custom reopen controls get the same with useSideNav().setOpen(true, { focus: true })
Preset with a custom header slot keeps a Toggle, so a closed rail can always be reopened

doNot: Do not invent Sidebar, SidebarHeader, SidebarNav, SidebarSection, SidebarItem, SidebarSubmenu, SidebarFooter, SidebarProvider, SidebarTrigger, SidebarContent, SidebarGroup, SidebarMenu, SidebarMenuItem, SidebarMenuButton, SidebarInset, or SidebarRail
Do not hand-roll nav rows (a, button, li with your own active/hover styles) inside SideNav — use SideNav.Item, which carries aria-current, the disclosure attributes and the closed-rail tooltip
Do not nest SideNav.Item deeper than one level, or put rows outside a SideNav.Section
Do not use SideNav.Root without a SideNav.Toggle or SideNav.Brand in its header when the rail can close — nothing would reopen it
Do not compose AppNav inside SideNav
Do not use Drawer for persistent app chrome
Do not use AppNav as closeable product chrome
Do not leave a gap between AppHeader and SideNav — radius none, showHeader false, layout-app with no gap
Do not give SideNav itself position:fixed, an overlay, a focus trap, or Escape-to-close; for narrow screens use AppShellPattern, which renders SideNav inside kit Drawer
Do not hand-roll a narrow-screen menu (hamburger, bottom tab bar, collapsed rail); use AppShellPattern (app-shell)
Do not use the shadcn sidebar package
Do not set component variables to raw hex or primitive --color-* ramps — use semantic tokens
Do not borrow AppHeader.Mark / AppHeader.Title for a SideNav brand — use SideNav.Brand, which keeps the mark on the closed rail and reopens it
